s: Which ratio gives the Capacity Utilisation Factor (CUF) of a power plant?
o: Actual output to output at full rated power over the period
Output at full rated power to actual output
x: CUF is actual output divided by the output possible at full rated power over the relevant period.

s: What is the typical Capacity Utilisation Factor of wind power in India?
x: Wind CUF is about 36–40%, above solar (~21%) but well below coal (~85%).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Vertical-axis wind turbine – Higher efficiency than a horizontal-axis turbine
Horizontal-axis wind turbine – Rotor axis parallel to the wind
Horizontal-axis wind turbine – No yaw control needed
x: A HAWT has its rotor axis parallel to the wind and needs yaw control; VAWTs such as Darrieus and Savonius take wind from any direction but have lower efficiency.

s: According to the Betz limit, what is the maximum share of the wind's kinetic energy a turbine can capture?
x: The Betz limit caps the share of wind's kinetic energy a turbine can capture at 16/27, about 59.3%.

s: Darrieus and Savonius are designs of which type of wind turbine?
x: Darrieus and Savonius are vertical-axis (VAWT) designs, not HAWT.

s: With which power of wind speed does the power available to a wind turbine vary?
x: Turbine power varies with the cube of wind speed (and with swept area), not the square.

s: For which sites are IEC Class III wind turbines designed?
o: Sites with wind from any direction
x: IEC turbine classes are set by site wind speed: Class I for high-wind and Class III for low-wind sites.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about wind turbines?
o: HAWT has its axis parallel to the wind
VAWT takes wind from any direction
VAWT has higher efficiency than HAWT
x: VAWTs suit small sites and have lower efficiency; HAWT is the standard utility turbine.

s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of energy conversion in a wind turbine?
o: Kinetic energy - mechanical energy - electrical energy
Potential energy - kinetic energy - electrical energy
Chemical energy - thermal energy - electrical energy
Thermal energy - mechanical energy - electrical energy
x: Wind's kinetic energy turns the blades (mechanical energy), and the generator turns this into electrical energy.

s: On which date is Global Wind Day observed?
x: Global Wind Day is observed on 15 June.

s: What is Madhya Pradesh's rank in installed wind capacity (June 2026)?
x: Madhya Pradesh is seventh in installed wind capacity, not third; Karnataka is third.

s: Which State did Gujarat overtake in 2023 to become India's largest wind-power State?
x: Gujarat overtook Tamil Nadu in 2023 to become the largest wind-power State.

s: Which three countries are ahead of India in installed wind capacity?
x: India is 4th in installed wind capacity, after China, USA and Germany.

s: Which country ranks second in the world in installed wind-power capacity?
x: The top three are China, the United States of America and Germany, in that order.

s: Which State ranks second in installed wind capacity in India (June 2026)?
x: Gujarat is first (16,086 MW) and Tamil Nadu second (12,273 MW).

s: What does the National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy, 2018 promote?
o: Separate wind and solar plants on different grids
Wind turbines and solar PV at the same grid connection point
Replacing wind turbines with solar panels
Hybrid projects only for off-grid rural use
x: The policy promotes co-location of wind turbines and solar PV at the same point of grid connection.

s: What type of facility does Ramagiri in Andhra Pradesh host?
x: Ramagiri hosts a hybrid solar-wind park.

s: In which year did SECI issue India's first round-the-clock (RTC) renewable power tender?
x: The first round-the-clock RE tender was issued by SECI in 2020, bundling RE with thermal power.

s: Under round-the-clock tenders, at least what share of annual energy must come from renewables?
x: RTC tenders require at least 51% of annual energy from renewables, including storage.

s: Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) charges were waived for renewable projects commissioned by which date?
x: ISTS charges were waived for projects commissioned by 30 June 2025.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Hybrid policy is 2018; offshore policy 2015, repowering 2016 and offshore VGF 2024.

s: Which of the following correctly matches the hub height with the assessed wind potential?
x: The assessed potential is 695.5 GW at a 120-metre hub height and 1,163.9 GW at a 150-metre hub height.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE)?
o: It prepares the Indian Wind Atlas
It supports testing and certification of wind technologies
It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Power
It undertakes wind-resource assessment and site identification
x: NIWE is an autonomous body under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, not the Ministry of Power.

s: Where is the National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) headquartered?
x: NIWE is located in Chennai and functions as an autonomous body under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

s: Which body prepares India's Wind Atlas?
x: NIWE does wind resource assessment and prepares the Wind Atlas.

s: In how many windy States does nearly two-thirds of India's wind capacity lie?
x: Nearly two-thirds of India's wind capacity is in 8 windy states, from Rajasthan and Gujarat to Tamil Nadu and Telangana.

s: Under which ministry is the National Institute of Wind Energy an autonomous body?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
x: NIWE, Chennai, is an autonomous body under MNRE, not the Ministry of Power.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of India's eight windy States that hold nearly two-thirds of the wind capacity?
x: The eight windy States are Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana; Kerala is not one.

s: Which State has the highest wind power potential at 120 m above ground level, according to NIWE?
x: At 120 m hub height Gujarat has the highest wind potential, about 142.56 GW, followed by Rajasthan and Karnataka.

s: What is the wind power potential of Andhra Pradesh at 120 m above ground level?
x: NIWE puts Andhra Pradesh's wind potential at about 74.90 GW at 120 m hub height. Gujarat is highest at 142.56 GW.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's installed wind-power capacity?
o: It first crossed 50 GW in March 2014
x: Capacity was only 21.04 GW in March 2014; it crossed 50 GW in March 2025.

s: What are India's annual wind turbine manufacturing capacity and its approximate degree of indigenisation respectively?
x: The wind-turbine manufacturing base has a capacity of about 24 GW per year, with 70–80% indigenisation.

s: What was India's installed wind capacity on 31 March 2014?
x: Installed wind was 21.04 GW on 31 March 2014 and rose 2.66 times to 56.09 GW by 31 March 2026.

s: Where does wind now rank among India's renewable energy sources?
o: Third, after solar and large hydro
x: Wind is India's second-largest RE source after solar, just ahead of large hydro.

s: In which year did India make its record annual wind capacity addition of 6.05 GW?
x: A record 6.05 GW of wind was added in FY2025-26, 46% above FY25.

s: What share of India's total installed power capacity did wind account for in 2026?
x: Wind was about 10.5% of total installed capacity in 2026; solar was about 29%.

s: What was India's installed wind power capacity in August 2026?
x: India's installed wind capacity was 58.14 GW in August 2026, up from 21.04 GW in 2014.

s: What is India's national target for installed wind capacity by 2030?
x: The national target is to reach 100 GW of installed wind capacity by 2030.

s: What is the stated offshore-wind capacity target for India by 2030?
x: India’s stated offshore-wind target is 30 GW by 2030.

s: India's 2015 renewable-energy goal of 175 GW by 2022 included how much wind capacity?
x: The 2015 goal was 175 GW of RE by 2022, including 60 GW of wind. 100 GW is the wind target for 2030, 30 GW is the offshore wind target for 2030, and 40 GW was the rooftop part of the 100 GW solar target, not wind.

s: India's NDC goal of 50% installed power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030 was:
x: The 50% non-fossil capacity goal was met early, at 51.93% by December 2025. 40% was the older NDC level, the target was not deferred, and 75% is not a stated figure.

s: For which year is India's long-term target of 155 GW of wind capacity set?
x: India's long-term goal is 155 GW of wind by 2035; 100 GW is the 2030 target.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's energy targets:
1. The 2015 NDC sought 40% non-fossil installed capacity by 2030.
2. The overall goal is 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.
3. The offshore wind target for 2030 is 100 GW.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 30 GW is the offshore target; 100 GW is total wind by 2030.

s: Which one of the following statements about onshore and offshore wind power is NOT correct?
o: Offshore projects eliminate all environmental and navigational risks.
Floating turbines can be used in deep water.
Offshore sites generally have stronger and steadier winds.
Onshore projects are generally cheaper and easier to maintain.
x: Offshore projects do not eliminate risks; they may involve corrosion, undersea cables, navigation issues and marine-ecology concerns.

s: Why do offshore wind farms have a higher capacity factor than onshore farms?
x: Offshore winds are stronger and steadier, giving a higher capacity factor; offshore is costlier and harder to maintain.

s: Which of the following is a problem mainly of offshore, not onshore, wind farms?
x: Rusting, undersea cables, navigation and marine ecology are offshore issues; land conflict and variable winds are onshore issues.

s: Between the coasts of which States does the 2024 offshore wind Viability Gap Funding scheme split its first 1 GW equally?
x: The 2024 offshore wind VGF scheme covers the first 1 GW, with 500 MW each off Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

s: Off the coasts of which States are India's initial offshore wind development zones located?
x: The identified zones are off the Gujarat coast and the Tamil Nadu coast, including the Gulf of Mannar.

s: Which is the nodal agency under the National Offshore Wind Energy Policy, 2015?
x: MNRE is the nodal ministry and NIWE, not SECI, is the nodal agency for offshore wind farms in India's EEZ.

s: What is the outlay of the 2024 offshore wind Viability Gap Funding scheme?
x: The 2024 offshore VGF scheme provides ₹7,453 crore for the first 1 GW.

s: In which maritime zone of India does the National Offshore Wind Energy Policy, 2015 provide for offshore wind farms?
x: The National Offshore Wind Energy Policy, 2015 is the framework for offshore wind farms in India's EEZ.

s: With which country did India set up an Offshore Wind Taskforce in February 2026?
x: The India-UK Offshore Wind Taskforce was set up in February 2026 (Vision 2035); Denmark's cooperation dates from 2019.

s: What does repowering of a wind turbine mean?
o: Moving an old turbine to a different State without changing its equipment
Converting a wind farm entirely into a solar park
Reducing the height and capacity of existing turbines
Replacing ageing turbines with larger and modern turbines at the same site
x: Repowering replaces ageing, less efficient turbines with more powerful modern units at the same windy site to increase generation.

s: As which policy was the National Repowering Policy, 2016 revised?
x: The 2016 policy was revised as the Repowering and Life Extension Policy, 2023.

s: Which support for wind energy sets obligations up to 2030?
x: The Wind RPO trajectory runs to 2030, alongside supports like accelerated depreciation and GBI.

s:
Arrange the following wind-energy policies in chronological order:
1. National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy
2. National Offshore Wind Energy Policy
3. Repowering and Life Extension Policy
4. National Repowering Policy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Offshore policy 2015, Repowering 2016, Hybrid 2018 and Repowering and Life Extension 2023.

s: Where is the principal wind-farm cluster of Andhra Pradesh located?
o: North Coastal Andhra around Srikakulam and Vizianagaram
Coastal Andhra around Kakinada and Machilipatnam
Rayalaseema, particularly Ananthapuramu, Kurnool and YSR Kadapa
x: Wind farms are concentrated in Rayalaseema, especially in Ananthapuramu, Kurnool and YSR Kadapa districts.

s: Which company is identified as the largest wind developer in Andhra Pradesh, with more than 1,700 MW?
x: Suzlon is identified as Andhra Pradesh's largest wind developer, with more than 1,700 MW.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank in installed wind capacity (June 2026)?
x: Andhra Pradesh, with 4,461 MW, is 6th in India in installed wind capacity (June 2026).

s: In Andhra Pradesh, wind ranks second among renewables after which source?
x: Wind, at 4,397.67 MW in 2025-26, is AP's second-largest RE source after solar.

s: In biomass gasification, biomass is heated with limited oxygen. What does the resulting syngas mainly consist of?
o: Carbon monoxide, hydrogen and carbon dioxide
Sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide and ammonia
x: Controlled or limited-oxygen gasification produces syngas containing carbon monoxide, hydrogen and carbon dioxide.

s: Producer gas is a mixture of carbon monoxide, hydrogen, carbon dioxide and which other gas?
x: Producer gas is a mix of CO, H₂, CO₂ and methane.

s: What is Compressed Biogas (CBG)?
o: Unpurified biogas stored at atmospheric pressure
Compressed carbon dioxide used as a fuel
Purified and compressed biogas chemically identical to CNG
x: CBG is purified and compressed biogas. Chemically, it is identical to compressed natural gas and is considered renewable and carbon-neutral.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a Microbial Fuel Cell?
o: It cleans wastewater and generates electricity simultaneously
Microorganisms in it act as catalysts
It converts the chemical energy of organic substrates into electricity
It burns organic matter to raise steam for a turbine
x: A microbial fuel cell does not burn anything: its microbes convert the chemical energy of organic matter directly into electricity while cleaning wastewater.

s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Food-processing residues are biomass sources relevant to waste.
II. Human sewage is a biomass source relevant to waste.
III. Biogenic municipal solid waste is a biomass source relevant to waste.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three are biomass sources from waste: food-processing residues, human sewage and the biological part of municipal waste.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about biogas?
o: Methane makes up about 85–95% of biogas
It is mainly methane and CO2 from anaerobic digestion of organic matter
Its methane is formed by methanogenic archaea in the absence of oxygen
The slurry left after digestion is a good organic manure
x: Methane is about 50–75% of biogas; 85–95% is the methane share of piped natural gas.

s: Which organisation popularised the 'Gramalakshmi' floating-drum gobar gas plant of Jashbhai Patel?
x: The 1950s Gramalakshmi plant was popularised by KVIC, not MNRE.

s: Which of the following describes biomass energy?
o: Solar energy stored by plants through photosynthesis
Energy obtained from tidal currents alone
Heat stored only in the Earth's mantle
x: Biomass energy represents solar energy captured and stored by plants through photosynthesis. It may be burned directly or converted into biogas and biofuels.

s: Which of the following is an example of biomass energy?
x: Gobar gas is biomass energy because it is produced from organic material, especially cattle dung.

s: Which microbes produce biogas through anaerobic digestion?
x: Biogas comes from anaerobic digestion by methanogens in the absence of oxygen.

s: What does bagasse cogeneration in sugar mills produce?
x: In bagasse cogeneration, sugar mills burn bagasse to produce steam and power together.

s: For what is the slurry left after biogas production used?
x: The slurry left after biogas production is a good organic manure.

s: What is the approximate methane content of biogas?
x: Biogas is about 50–75% methane; piped natural gas is 85–95% methane.

s: Which microorganism is associated with the production of bioethanol by fermentation of sugar or starch?
x: Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a yeast, ferments sugars or starch-derived sugars to produce bioethanol.

s: What is power alcohol?
o: Fuel-grade ethanol made mainly from molasses
Biodiesel made exclusively from palm stearin oil
Hydrogen produced by electrolysis of water
x: Power alcohol refers to fuel-grade ethanol, which in India is made mainly from molasses, a by-product of the sugar industry.

s: What is the mixture of petrol and ethanol, usually with about 10% ethanol, called?
x: Gasohol is petrol (gasoline) blended with ethanol, typically about 10% ethanol.

s: Which is the principal feedstock for ethanol in the United States, the world's largest ethanol producer?
x: The US mainly uses maize or corn for ethanol, whereas Brazil mainly uses sugarcane.

s: In which year did Brazil make ethanol blending mandatory?
x: Brazil has mandated ethanol blending since 1976 and has used about 25% ethanol since 2007.

s: Which renewable can supply 24×7 baseload power, as it does not depend on sunlight or wind?
x: Geothermal energy comes from underground heat that does not depend on sunlight or wind, so it can supply 24×7 baseload power.

s: India's National Policy on Geothermal Energy (2025) provides for how many pilot projects?
x: The policy, notified by MNRE on 15 September 2025, has five pilot projects, not ten.

s: In which State is the Surajkund geothermal field located?
x: Surajkund geothermal field is in Jharkhand; Tapovan is in Uttarakhand and Puga Valley in Ladakh.

s: Which of the following is NOT a listed geothermal province or region of India?
x: The listed geothermal regions include the Himalaya, Godavari Valley, Cambay, SONATA, Mahanadi, West Coast and Andaman-Nicobar. The Indo-Gangetic Plain is not included in that list.

s: What are Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) designed to do?
o: Prevent all water movement in geothermal fields
Convert solar radiation directly into electricity
Replace radioactive decay with chemical combustion
x: EGS technology artificially stimulates geothermal reservoirs to improve access to underground heat.

s: What is India's geothermal potential as estimated by the Geological Survey of India?
x: India's estimated geothermal potential is about 10,600 MW from 381 hot springs, according to the stated GSI estimate.

s: Hot springs, geysers and volcanoes are surface signs of which form of energy?
x: They are surface expressions of heat originating within the Earth, i.e. geothermal energy.

s: What is the primary source of geothermal energy?
o: Heat from the Earth's interior, largely associated with radioactive decay
Chemical energy released by surface oxidation
x: Geothermal energy originates from the internal heat of the Earth, much of which is generated by radioactive decay in its interior.

s: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge associated with geothermal energy?
o: Subsidence and water pollution from geothermal fluids
x: The stated challenges are uneven reservoir distribution, high drilling costs, subsidence and water pollution from geothermal fluids. Geothermal energy necessarily depends on underground heat.

s: Where was the world's first geothermal power generated in 1904?
x: The world's first geothermal power was generated at Larderello, Italy, in 1904; Puga is India's first project.

s: Which geothermal field–State pair is correctly matched?
x: Tattapani is in Chhattisgarh; Manikaran is in Himachal, Tapovan in Uttarakhand and Surajkund in Jharkhand.

s: The Manuguru geothermal site belongs to which geothermal province?
x: Manuguru (old Khammam district, now Telangana) is a Godavari valley geothermal site.

s: Which Ministry issued India's first National Policy on Geothermal Energy (September 2025)?
x: India's first National Policy on Geothermal Energy was issued by MNRE on 15 September 2025.

s: Which company took up India's first geothermal power project at Puga in Ladakh?
x: ONGC is developing India's first geothermal project at Puga, Ladakh; its MoU was extended for five years in May 2026.

s: Which geothermal area of India has the highest geothermal potential?
x: Puga Valley and Chumathang in Ladakh have the highest geothermal potential in India.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Geothermal field)
A. Tapovan
B. Manikaran
C. Tattapani
D. Surajkund
List-II (State)
1. Chhattisgarh
2. Jharkhand
3. Uttarakhand
4. Himachal Pradesh
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Tapovan is in Uttarakhand, Manikaran in Himachal Pradesh, Tattapani in Chhattisgarh and Surajkund in Jharkhand.

s: Puga in Ladakh, site of India's first geothermal project, is also described as which of the following?
o: The world's first geothermal power plant
x: Puga (ONGC) is India's first geothermal project and the world's highest, at about 14,000 ft; Larderello in Italy was the world's first.

s: Biodiesel is commercially produced by which of the following processes?
o: Pyrolysis of lignocellulosic residues without a catalyst
Transesterification of vegetable oils or animal fats with methanol or ethanol
Fermentation of starch by methanogenic bacteria
Electrolysis of water in the presence of vegetable oil
x: Biodiesel is produced by transesterifying vegetable oils or animal fats with methanol or ethanol, producing fatty-acid methyl or ethyl esters.

s: Which feedstock accounts for about 94% of India's biodiesel?
x: Palm stearin oil accounts for about 94% of India's biodiesel feedstock.

s: What is India's target for biodiesel blending in diesel by 2030?
x: India targets 5% biodiesel blending by 2030; actual blending remains below 0.5%.

s: What is the botanical name of Karanja, a biodiesel plant?
x: Karanja is Pongamia pinnata, a biodiesel plant with non-edible oil rich in oleic acid; Jatropha curcas is ratanjyot.

s: FSSAI's RUCO initiative turns which of the following into biodiesel?
x: RUCO (FSSAI) stands for Repurpose Used Cooking Oil, for making biodiesel.

s: What is India's present level of biodiesel blending in diesel?
x: India's biodiesel blend is still below 0.5%; the target is 5% by 2030.

s: Where did the Belgian firm VITO launch a two-year biodiesel project in April 2023?
x: In April 2023 the Belgian firm VITO launched a two-year biodiesel project at Ayodhya.

s: Which plant, known as 'ratanjyot', is grown as a non-edible biodiesel crop?
x: Jatropha curcas (ratanjyot) is a biodiesel plant; its non-edible seeds contain about 40% oil.

s: Which is India's lead ocean-energy research body?
x: The National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, is the lead ocean-energy research body.

s: Where was India's first wave-energy plant established?
x: India's first wave-power pilot was established at Vizhinjam, Kerala, in 1991.

s: Which of the following sites has the greatest tidal-energy potential among the listed Indian sites?
x: The Gulf of Khambhat in Gujarat is identified as India's best tidal-energy site, with an estimated potential of about 7,000 MW.

s: About what temperature difference between surface and deep water does Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) need?
x: OTEC needs about a 20°C difference and is viable mainly between 30°N and 30°S.

s: Which of the following is identified as an OTEC location in India?
x: Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are OTEC locations; the Gulfs of Khambhat and Kutch are tidal-energy sites.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Durgaduani Creek tidal pilot is in the Sundarbans; Vizhinjam is in Kerala.

s: What tidal range does a site need to be suitable for tidal power?
x: Tidal power needs a tidal range of about 5 m or more in a narrow gulf or estuary.

s: Which of the following is NOT a tidal-energy site of India?
x: The Gulf of Mannar is an offshore wind zone, not a tidal site; Khambhat, Kutch and the Sundarbans are tidal sites.

s: Under which of the following does the National Institute of Ocean Technology, Chennai, function?
x: NIOT, Chennai, India's lead ocean-energy body, is under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

s: Where is Durgaduani Creek, a proposed tidal-power pilot site?
x: Durgaduani Creek, a proposed tidal pilot, is in the Sundarbans, West Bengal.

s: Where was India's first Low Temperature Thermal Desalination (LTTD) plant set up by NIOT in 2005?
x: NIOT, Chennai set up India's first LTTD desalination plant at Kavaratti, Lakshadweep in 2005, giving 1 lakh litres of water a day.

s: About how much fresh water per day does the LTTD desalination plant at Kavaratti produce?
x: The Kavaratti LTTD plant (2005) of NIOT produces about 1 lakh litres of drinking water per day.

s: What is the identified tidal energy potential of India as estimated by MNRE?
x: MNRE puts India's tidal potential at about 12,455 MW, mainly in the Khambhat and Kutch regions of Gujarat; wave potential is about 40,000 MW.

s: What is the estimated wave energy potential along India's coast?
x: MNRE estimates India's wave energy potential at about 40,000 MW; OTEC potential is about 1,80,000 MW.

s: Unlike direct ethanol blending, what does Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) use?
x: SAF uses drop-in synthesised hydrocarbons suited to aviation fuel systems, not simply direct ethanol.

s: What is India's Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) target for international flights by 2030?
x: The SAF roadmap sets 1% by 2027, 2% by 2028 and 5% by 2030, in line with ICAO's net-zero 2050 goal.

s: Which policy specifically supports bio-jet fuel among the following?
x: The BioE3 Policy 2024 supports bio-jet fuel.

s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The first airline biofuel flight was operated by SpiceJet.
II. The first biofuel flight was on the Dehradun–Delhi route.
III. The date of the first biofuel flight was 27 August 2018.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: SpiceJet flew India's first biofuel flight, from Dehradun to Delhi, on 27 August 2018.

s: At which forum was the Global Biofuels Alliance launched on 9 September 2023?
x: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched on 9 September 2023 at the G20 Summit, New Delhi.

s: Which countries are the core founding members of the Global Biofuels Alliance?
x: The core founders of the Global Biofuels Alliance are India, USA and Brazil; its Secretariat is in New Delhi.

s: Which was India's first ISCC CORSIA-certified Sustainable Aviation Fuel producer (August 2025)?
x: IOCL Panipat became India's first ISCC CORSIA-certified SAF producer in August 2025.

s: Up to what share can Sustainable Aviation Fuel be blended with conventional jet fuel?
x: SAF is a drop-in synthesised hydrocarbon that can be blended up to 50% with jet fuel.

s: Where is the Secretariat of the Global Biofuels Alliance located?
x: Under a host agreement of October 2024, the Global Biofuels Alliance Secretariat is in New Delhi.

s: Which institute developed the jatropha-based bio-jet fuel used in India's first biofuel flight in August 2018?
x: SpiceJet's Dehradun–Delhi biofuel flight (27 August 2018) used jatropha bio-jet fuel from CSIR-Indian Institute of Petroleum, Dehradun.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's first biofuel flight:
1. It used bio-jet fuel made from jatropha.
2. It was flown in a Bombardier Q-400 aircraft.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The SpiceJet flight of 27 August 2018 was a Bombardier Q-400 running on jatropha bio-jet fuel from CSIR-IIP.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the generation of biofuel?
o: 2G — food crops such as sugarcane and corn
x: Third-generation biofuels use algae or algal biomass. First-generation fuels use food crops, second-generation fuels use non-food lignocellulosic material, and fourth-generation fuels use genetically engineered organisms.

s:
Assertion (A): Algae biofuel requires expertise, capital and large-scale facilities.
Reason (R): Algae can be grown on land that is unsuitable for agriculture.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: growing algae on non-farm land is an advantage, while the need for expertise, capital and large plants comes from the cost and complexity of cultivation and processing.

s: Which of the following feedstocks is characteristic of second-generation biofuels?
x: Second-generation biofuels use non-food lignocellulosic residues such as rice straw, straw, husk, wood chips and bamboo.

s: Which of the following is a limitation of algal biofuel?
x: Energy-intensive lipid extraction is a limitation; high yield and use of wastewater and CO2 are advantages.

s: Which microorganism is used to produce biobutanol?
x: Biobutanol is made with Clostridium acetobutylicum and has higher energy density than ethanol.

s: Under the National Policy on Biofuels 2018, whose approval is needed to use surplus food grains for ethanol production?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
x: Surplus food grains may be converted to ethanol only with NBCC approval (APPSC-G2 2025). FCI supplies the rice but does not approve; MNRE and NITI Aayog are not the approving body under the policy.

s: Beyond which traditional feedstock did the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018 widen the ethanol feedstock base?
x: The NPB 2018 widened ethanol feedstock beyond molasses by adding sugarcane juice, surplus FCI rice, maize and damaged foodgrains.

s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of the National Policy on Biofuels?
o: Discouraging the production of advanced biofuels
x: The National Policy on Biofuels aims to reduce import dependence, promote domestic feedstock, strengthen energy security and generate employment. It does not discourage advanced biofuels.

s: To which Ethanol Supply Year did the 2022 amendment to the National Policy on Biofuels advance the E20 target?
x: The 2018 policy aimed at E20 by 2030; the 2022 amendment advanced it to ESY 2025-26.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2022 amendment to the National Policy on Biofuels?
o: It barred the addition of new members to the NBCC
It permitted biofuel units in SEZs and EOUs under Make in India
It permitted exports in specific cases
x: The 2022 amendment allowed new members to be added to the NBCC, so saying it barred them is wrong. It also allowed more feedstocks, biofuel production in SEZs/EOUs under Make in India, and export of biofuels in specific cases.

s: Under the National Policy on Biofuels, which of the following is a 'basic' biofuel?
x: Basic biofuels are 1G bioethanol and biodiesel; 2G ethanol, drop-in fuels, 3G biofuels and bio-CNG are advanced biofuels.

s: Which section of the Motor Vehicles Act permits engine conversion to biofuels?
x: Section 52 of the Motor Vehicles Act permits conversion of engines to biofuels.

s: The Minister of which Ministry chairs the National Biofuel Coordination Committee?
o: Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
x: The NBCC is chaired by the Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Biofuel Coordination Committee:
1. It approved surplus FCI rice for ethanol in April 2020.
2. The 2022 amendment allowed new members to be added to it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: NBCC approved surplus FCI rice in April 2020, and the 2022 amendment allows new members to be added to it.

s: Under the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018, which of the following is an 'advanced' biofuel?
x: Advanced biofuels include 2G ethanol, drop-in fuels from MSW, 3G biofuels and bio-CNG; 1G bioethanol and biodiesel are basic.

s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a raw material for ethanol under the National Policy on Biofuels?
x: The policy allows cassava, sugar beet, rotten potatoes and damaged grains for ethanol; groundnut, an edible oilseed, is not listed.

s: How much Foreign Direct Investment is allowed under the automatic route for biofuel technology meant for domestic use?
x: Under the National Policy on Biofuels, 100% FDI is allowed through the automatic route for biofuel technology for domestic use; plantations are barred.

s: In the feedstock-wise pricing of ethanol bought by Oil Marketing Companies, what is the correct order from highest to lowest price?
x: Ethanol made from maize has the highest price, rice-based ethanol the lowest, and molasses-based ethanol lies between them.

s: From which date did E20 petrol with a minimum Research Octane Number of 95 become mandatory in India?
x: Mandatory E20 petrol with a minimum RON of 95 was scheduled from 1 April 2026.

s: The next ethanol-blending target after E20 is which of the following?
x: The next stated target is 30% ethanol blending, or E30, by 2030.

s: When did India achieve E10 ethanol blending in petrol?
x: After the 2001 pilot and E5 from 1 January 2003, E10 was achieved in June 2022; E20 is mandatory from 1 April 2026.

s: In the food-versus-fuel debate, the rise in maize area has been accompanied by a decline in the area under which crop?
x: Maize-ethanol pricing has been linked with diversion of land from pulses and oilseeds.

s: When did E5 ethanol blending in 9 States and 4 Union Territories begin?
x: E5 began in 9 States and 4 UTs on 1 January 2003, after a 2001 pilot.

s: Which Ministry runs India's Ethanol Blending Programme?
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
x: The Ethanol Blending Programme is run by MoPNG, with OMCs paying feedstock-wise prices.

s: Which BIS standard of 2026 covers higher ethanol blends of petrol such as E22, E25, E27 and E30?
x: BIS issued IS 19850:2026 in May 2026 for E22, E25, E27 and E30 petrol blends.

s: In waste-to-energy, what is heating waste in the absence of oxygen called?
x: Pyrolysis heats waste without oxygen; gasification is partial oxidation and incineration is direct burning.

s: Where are small hydro projects commonly developed?
o: Hill streams and canal falls only
Canal falls and toes of dams only
Hill streams, canal falls and toes of dams
x: Run-of-river small hydro may use hill streams, canal falls and water released at dam toes.

s: What is the capacity range of mini hydro plants in India?
o: Above 2 MW and up to 25 MW
x: Micro hydro is up to 100 kW, mini hydro 101 kW to 2 MW and small hydro above 2 MW up to 25 MW.

s: What is the upper capacity limit of a small hydro project in India?
x: Small hydro covers 2–25 MW; micro is up to 100 kW and mini up to 2 MW.

s: In which States does about half of India's small hydro potential lie?
o: Bihar, West Bengal, Odisha and Jharkhand
Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, J&K and Uttarakhand
Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Goa and Telangana
x: About half of India's small hydro potential is in Arunachal, Himachal, J&K and Uttarakhand.

s: Where is the Okhla waste-to-energy plant located?
x: Okhla, Ghazipur and Narela-Bawana are waste-to-energy plants in Delhi.

s: In biomethanation, what converts wet waste into biogas?
x: In biomethanation, microbes convert wet waste into biogas.

s: About what share of India's small hydro potential has been installed so far?
x: India's installed small hydro capacity is about 5.18 GW, which is only about 25% of its potential.

s: What is Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF)?
o: The dry combustible part of municipal solid waste
x: RDF is the dry, combustible fraction of municipal solid waste, used as fuel in waste-to-energy plants and cement kilns.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MNRE's classification of energy sources?
o: Bio-power includes biomass, bagasse cogeneration and waste-to-energy
Geothermal, tidal and OTEC are renewable sources under development
Nuclear capacity of 8.78 GW is counted separately
Nuclear power is classified as renewable energy
x: Nuclear power is non-fossil but not classified as renewable; its capacity is counted separately.

s: Since 2019, which source has been included in MNRE's renewable-energy classification?
x: Large hydro has been classified as renewable since 2019; nuclear is non-fossil but not renewable.

s: Which of the following is non-fossil but NOT counted as renewable by MNRE?
x: Nuclear is non-fossil but not renewable; large hydro is counted as renewable since 2019.

s: What does SATAT, launched in 2018 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, mainly promote?
o: CBG production from agricultural residue and municipal waste
Ethanol production only from imported crude oil
x: SATAT, or Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation, was launched in 2018 by MoPNG to promote CBG from agricultural residue and municipal waste.

s: In which year was GOBARdhan (Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan) launched?
x: GOBARdhan was launched in 2018, the same year as SATAT.

s: What is the Phase-I outlay of the National Bioenergy Programme (2021–2026)?
x: Phase-I (1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026) has an outlay of ₹858 crore, implemented by MNRE through State Nodal Agencies.

s: At what level did the Ministry of Power policy of 2021 mandate biomass co-firing in coal-based plants?
x: The 2021 policy mandated 5% biomass co-firing in coal plants, to rise to 7%.

s: Which institutional mechanism is associated with implementation of biomass co-firing in thermal power plants?
x: National Mission SAMARTH is associated with the biomass co-firing initiative in thermal power plants.

s: Up to which year does the revised PM JI-VAN Yojana extend?
x: The revised scheme covers advanced biofuels, including bolt-on and brownfield projects, up to 2028–29.

s: In which year was the PM JI-VAN Yojana launched?
x: PM JI-VAN Yojana was launched in 2019 to support 2G ethanol and subsequently expanded to advanced biofuels.

s: Where is the Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Bio-Energy, which inspects work under MNRE's National Bioenergy Programme, located?
x: SSS-NIBE is at Kapurthala, Punjab. Chennai hosts NIWE and NIOT, Gurugram hosts NISE, and Dehradun hosts CSIR-IIP - none is the bioenergy inspection body.

s: What is the compressed biogas obligation under SATAT from 2028-29?
x: Under SATAT the CBG obligation rises 1%/3%/4% over FY26-28 and is 5% from 2028-29.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Co-firing is under the Ministry of Power (SAMARTH); SATAT is MoPNG, the National Bioenergy Programme is MNRE and PM JI-VAN is 2019.

s: Which policy of Andhra Pradesh supports biofuels as part of its clean-energy approach?
x: The AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024 supports biofuels.

s: Where did Reliance lay the foundation of its first compressed biogas plant in April 2025?
x: Reliance laid the foundation of its first CBG plant at Kanigiri, Prakasam, on 2 April 2025.

s: Which company runs the waste-to-energy plants at Naidupalem (Guntur) and Kapuluppada (Visakhapatnam)?
x: Jindal (JITF) runs WtE plants at Naidupalem, Guntur and Kapuluppada, Visakhapatnam.

s: Reliance's Kanigiri CBG plant uses which feedstock grown on barren land?
x: The Kanigiri CBG plant uses Napier grass grown on barren land.

s: Among the following bio-energy sources, which has the largest installed capacity in Andhra Pradesh as per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26?
x: AP has bagasse cogeneration of 206.95 MW, biomass 171.25 MW, small hydro 106.80 MW and MSW power 36.15 MW.

s: Where is India's first commercial-scale bamboo bioethanol plant, dedicated on 14 September 2025?
x: Numaligarh (Golaghat, Assam) is India's first commercial bamboo bioethanol plant, dedicated on 14 September 2025. Panipat is the first commercial 2G plant; Bathinda and Bargarh are other 2G plants.

s: Which of the following 2G ethanol plants is wrongly matched?
x: HPCL Bathinda is in Punjab; Bargarh is the Odisha plant.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Panipat is the first commercial 2G plant; Larderello is the world geothermal first, Puga the Indian geothermal first and Numaligarh the first 2G bamboo plant.

s: Within what range of concentration by volume does hydrogen burn in air?
x: Hydrogen is flammable in air over a wide range of about 4% to 75% by volume.

s: Green ammonia is produced by combining which of the following?
x: Green ammonia is produced from nitrogen and green hydrogen. It is important for fertiliser production and can also serve as a fuel and marine fuel.

s: Why is hydrogen especially useful in sectors such as steel, shipping and fertilisers?
x: Hydrogen suits hard-to-abate sectors like steel, shipping and fertilisers, where direct electrification is difficult.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about applications of green hydrogen in India?
o: Hydrogen blending in city-gas networks is being evaluated as H-CNG
Fuel-cell trucks, buses and ships are potential applications
It is not being considered for steel
Long-duration energy storage is a potential application
x: Green hydrogen is being considered for fertilisers, refineries and steel.

s: Which of the following is an industrial, not a fuel or transport, use of hydrogen?
x: Ammonia for fertiliser is an industrial use; fuel-cell vehicles, rocket fuel and CNG blending are fuel uses.

s: How does hydrogen help decarbonise steel production?
o: Direct reduced iron replacing coking coal
x: Steel uses hydrogen-based direct reduced iron in place of coking coal.

s: What does H-CNG refer to?
o: Hydrogen made from CNG by reforming
x: H-CNG is hydrogen blended into CNG or city gas, a fuel use of hydrogen.

s: For what is hydrogen mainly used in oil refineries?
x: In refining, hydrogen is used for desulphurisation.

s: What is hydrogen that occurs naturally through geological processes called?
x: White hydrogen is naturally occurring geological hydrogen.

s: Pink hydrogen is produced by electrolysis using which of the following?
x: Pink hydrogen comes from electrolysis powered by nuclear energy.

s: Which of the following describes blue hydrogen?
x: Blue hydrogen captures CO₂ for low emissions; grey releases it, green has zero and brown/black very high emissions.

s: What is hydrogen produced from natural gas with carbon capture and storage called?
x: That is blue hydrogen; green hydrogen comes from electrolysis using renewable power.

s: Methane pyrolysis (natural gas heated without oxygen) produces which type of hydrogen?
x: Methane pyrolysis gives turquoise hydrogen; steam methane reforming gives grey or blue and renewable electrolysis green.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Grey hydrogen – Electrolysis using renewable electricity
Green hydrogen – Steam reforming of natural gas
Grey hydrogen – Steam reforming of natural gas
x: Grey hydrogen, about 95% of production today, comes from steam reforming of natural gas with CO₂ released; green hydrogen comes from electrolysis using renewable power.

s: What is the approximate cost of green hydrogen compared with grey hydrogen?
o: Green hydrogen: about $4 per kg; grey hydrogen: $1.5–2 per kg
Green hydrogen: $0.5 per kg; grey hydrogen: $1.5–2 per kg
Green hydrogen: $1.5–2 per kg; grey hydrogen: about $4 per kg
Both green and grey hydrogen: $4 per kg
x: Green hydrogen is estimated at about $4 per kg, whereas grey hydrogen costs approximately $1.5–2 per kg.

s: What is hydrogen made by coal gasification without carbon capture called?
x: Brown/black hydrogen comes from coal gasification without CCS, the dirtiest route.

s: Which catalyst is used in steam methane reforming?
x: In SMR, methane and steam react at 700–1000°C over a nickel catalyst.

s: How is green hydrogen mainly produced?
o: Steam methane reforming of natural gas
Electrolysis of water using renewable power
Electrolysis of water using nuclear power
x: Green hydrogen comes from electrolysis of water using renewable power (PYQ 2023) and is the only zero-carbon colour. Steam methane reforming gives grey, methane pyrolysis gives turquoise, and nuclear-powered electrolysis gives pink hydrogen.

s: Which type of hydrogen, made by steam methane reforming, is the cheapest and accounts for about 95% of present production?
x: Grey hydrogen from steam methane reforming of natural gas is the cheapest and makes up about 95% of production.

s: Which of the following describes India's first hydrogen train in service?
o: A shuttle bus operating at Central Vista, Delhi, from 2022
A ferry launched from Cochin Shipyard Limited in 2024
A 10-coach train operating on the Jind-Sonipat route in Haryana from July 2026
A single coach tested at Chennai’s ICF in 2025
x: The first hydrogen fuel-cell train in service is described as a 10-coach train on the 89-km Jind-Sonipat route in Haryana from July 2026. It is identified as the world’s longest and most powerful broad-gauge hydrogen train.

s: The first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell ferry in India was built by which organisation?
x: The first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell ferry was built by Cochin Shipyard Limited. It was a fully indigenous LT-PEM fuel-cell ferry.

s: The hydrogen-powered coach tested by the Railways was associated with which location and organisation?
x: The first hydrogen-powered train coach tested by the Railways was associated with Chennai’s Integral Coach Factory (ICF). This is distinct from the hydrogen train in service associated with Jind-Sonipat.

s: Who developed India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell bus (2022)?
x: The first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell bus was developed by KPIT with CSIR-NCL, Pune, in 2022.

s: Students of which university built and drove the world's first hydrogen fuel-cell car to reach Sydney (27 December 2003)?
x: It was built and driven by students of Tamagawa University, Tokyo (PYQ 2004). The other institutions are not linked to this run.

s: Which company introduced H-CNG buses in Delhi in 2020?
x: H-CNG buses were run in Delhi by IOCL in 2020.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Hydrogen mobility first)
A. First indigenous fuel-cell ferry
B. Hydrogen train coach tested
C. First indigenous fuel-cell bus (2022)
D. H-CNG buses in Delhi (2020)
List-II (Builder / Site)
1. ICF, Chennai
2. IOCL
3. Cochin Shipyard Ltd
4. KPIT with CSIR-NCL, Pune
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Cochin Shipyard built the fuel-cell ferry, ICF Chennai tested the hydrogen coach, KPIT with CSIR-NCL made the bus and IOCL ran H-CNG buses in Delhi.

s: In a PEM fuel cell, where is hydrogen split into protons and electrons?
x: Hydrogen splits at the anode; protons cross the membrane to the cathode and electrons flow through the external circuit.

s: Besides electricity, what does a fuel cell produce from hydrogen and oxygen?
x: A fuel cell converts hydrogen and oxygen electrochemically into electricity and water, with zero emissions at the point of use.

s: In a PEM fuel cell, which particles cross the membrane to the cathode?
x: In a PEM fuel cell, protons cross the membrane while electrons flow through the external circuit.

s: What is the total outlay approved for the National Green Hydrogen Mission up to 2029-30?
x: The Mission has a total outlay of ₹19,744 crore up to financial year 2029-30.

s: What is the full form of SHIP under the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
x: SHIP is the Strategic Hydrogen Innovation Partnership, a PPP for R&D.

s: Which is the nodal ministry of the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
x: MNRE is the nodal ministry; BEE under the Ministry of Power handles only certification.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated 2030 target of the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
o: Production of 5 million metric tonnes of green hydrogen annually
Addition of 125 GW of renewable energy capacity
x: The Mission targets 60-100 GW of electrolyser capacity, not 200 GW. The other three figures are stated 2030 targets.

s: How much green hydrogen per year does the National Green Hydrogen Mission aim to produce by 2030?
x: The Mission targets 5 MMT a year by 2030, possibly reaching 10 MMT including exports.

s: About how many jobs is the National Green Hydrogen Mission expected to create by 2030?
x: The Mission expects about 6 lakh jobs, over ₹8 lakh crore investment and about 50 MMT annual GHG reduction.

s: By which year does India aim to reach net zero?
x: India's net-zero target is 2070; 2047 is linked with energy independence.

s: Companies of which country signed long-term green ammonia and green methanol export agreements with India?
x: India signed long-term green ammonia and green methanol export agreements with Japanese companies.

s: What does SIGHT under the National Green Hydrogen Mission provide?
o: Incentives for electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production
A National Centre for Hydrogen Safety
x: SIGHT gives two incentives, for electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production; SHIP is the R&D partnership.

s: What is the outlay for SIGHT under the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
x: SIGHT has ₹17,490 crore of the ₹19,744 crore mission outlay; pilots get ₹1,466 crore and SHIP ₹400 crore.

s: How many companies have been awarded 3,000 MW of electrolyser manufacturing capacity under the Mission?
x: 15 companies have been awarded 3,000 MW of electrolyser manufacturing capacity (Aug 2026).

s: What is the National Green Hydrogen Mission's 2030 target for electrolyser capacity?
x: The 2030 electrolyser target is 60–100 GW, not 200 GW; 125 GW is the added RE target.

s: When did the Union Cabinet approve the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
x: The Union Cabinet approved the National Green Hydrogen Mission on 4 January 2023, with MNRE as the nodal ministry.

s: By which year does India aim to achieve energy independence, a goal of the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
x: The Mission's goals are energy independence by 2047 and net zero by 2070.

s: At what price per kg did SECI discover the tariff for 7,24,000 TPA of green ammonia, among the world's lowest?
x: SECI's tender for 7,24,000 tonnes a year of green ammonia discovered about ₹53.27 per kg, among the world's lowest.

s: How many Hydrogen Valley Innovation Clusters have been sanctioned under the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
x: Four Hydrogen Valley Innovation Clusters (₹170 crore) have been set up, along with a National Centre for Hydrogen Safety.

s: How much reduction in greenhouse gas emissions per year is the National Green Hydrogen Mission expected to bring by 2030?
x: The Mission expects a cut of about 50 MMT of GHG emissions a year and investment of over ₹8 lakh crore by 2030.

s: Which port–State pair is correctly matched?
x: V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin) is in Tamil Nadu; Deendayal (Kandla) is in Gujarat and Paradip in Odisha.

s: In which State is the Deendayal (Kandla) green hydrogen hub port?
x: Deendayal (Kandla) port, a green hydrogen hub, is in Gujarat.

s: In which State is V.O. Chidambaranar Port, which has a ₹35 crore green hydrogen bunkering pilot?
x: V.O. Chidambaranar Port is in Tamil Nadu, not Odisha.

s: Where was the Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration of Andhra Pradesh (19 July 2025) made?
x: The declaration was made at Amaravati to make AP India's green hydrogen capital.

s: Which institution is the state nodal agency for the Andhra Pradesh Green Hydrogen Valley?
x: SRM University-AP is the state nodal agency for the Andhra Pradesh Green Hydrogen Valley.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pudimadaka — NTPC Green Energy green hydrogen hub
Simhadri — Seawater-to-hydrogen plant and blending trials
Amaravati — Paradip green ammonia export terminal
x: Amaravati is associated with the Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration, not a Paradip green ammonia export terminal. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Where is NTPC Green Energy's green hydrogen hub in Andhra Pradesh?
x: NTPC Green Energy's hub is at Pudimadaka, Anakapalli; its foundation was laid in January 2025.

s: Where is AM Green's green ammonia plant in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AM Green's green ammonia plant is at Kakinada.

s: What 2030 green hydrogen goal does the Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration of Andhra Pradesh set?
x: The Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration set AP a goal of 1.5 MMTPA by 2030 plus 5 GW of electrolyser manufacturing.

s: Which is the nodal agency of the Andhra Pradesh Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy (2023)?
x: NREDCAP is the nodal agency of the AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy (2023); SRM University-AP is the valley's nodal body.

s: Which group consists only of chemical carriers used to transport hydrogen for export?
x: Ammonia, methanol and liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHC) are chemical carriers for transporting hydrogen.

s: Which of the following is a recognised challenge for green hydrogen in India?
o: No need for water in production
x: Import dependence on electrolysers is a recognised challenge for green hydrogen, along with high cost compared with grey hydrogen, cryogenic transport and water stress.

s: Which institution is the nodal authority for certification under the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
x: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency, under the Ministry of Power, is the nodal authority for certification.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Green Hydrogen Standard of August 2023:
1. Well-to-gate emissions must not exceed 2 kg CO2-eq per kg of hydrogen.
2. The emissions are calculated as a 12-month average.
3. It was notified by the Ministry of Power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Standard allows not more than 2 kg CO2-eq per kg H2 as a 12-month average. Statement 3 is wrong: it was notified by MNRE.

s: When was the Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India (GHCI) launched?
x: The Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India was launched in April 2025.

s:
Consider the following statements about PEM electrolysers:
1. They use a solid polymer membrane.
2. Their quick response suits variable renewable energy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: a PEM electrolyser uses a solid polymer membrane and its quick response suits variable renewable energy.

s: What does an electrolyser do?
o: Combines nitrogen and hydrogen to produce electricity
Splits water into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity
Converts hydrogen directly into crude oil
x: An electrolyser uses electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen.

s: Which electrolyser uses high-temperature steam and is the most efficient?
x: Solid oxide electrolysers use high-temperature steam and are the most efficient.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about electrolysers?
o: Alkaline electrolysers use a liquid KOH/NaOH electrolyte
PEM electrolysers use a solid polymer membrane
Solid oxide electrolysers use high-temperature steam
x: AEM electrolysers can use non-platinum catalysts such as nickel, cobalt and iron.

s: Dominance of which country is a major concern in India's electrolyser supply chain?
x: A key concern in electrolyser supply is Chinese dominance.

s: Which method stores hydrogen for vehicle use in the solid state?
x: Hydrogen can be held in the solid state in metal hydrides; compressed gas and liquid hydrogen are gas and cryogenic-liquid forms, and ammonia is a chemical carrier.

s: About how much purified water is required to produce one kilogram of hydrogen through electrolysis?
x: Approximately 9 litres of purified water are required per kilogram of hydrogen, which can constrain projects in arid solar regions.

s: At about what temperature is liquid hydrogen stored?
x: Liquid hydrogen is kept at about −253°C; its very low density (about 0.071 g/ml) needs large tanks.

s: During the discharge of an electrochemical cell, where does oxidation occur?
x: Oxidation (loss of electrons) occurs at the anode and reduction (gain of electrons) at the cathode.

s: In a battery, what does the electrolyte allow to move between the electrodes?
x: An electrolyte lets ions flow and keeps the electrodes apart; it does not provide a direct electronic path.

s: Which process takes place at the cathode of a cell during discharge?
x: During discharge the cathode gains electrons, which is reduction; oxidation (loss of electrons) occurs at the anode.

s: The use of nickel-cadmium batteries has declined partly because of the toxicity of which metal?
x: Ni-Cd batteries are rechargeable but have become less common because cadmium is toxic.

s: Which non-rechargeable cell is commonly used in torches and clocks?
x: The zinc-carbon dry cell is generally non-rechargeable and common in torches and clocks.

s: Which battery chemistry–application pair is correctly matched?
o: Lead-acid – grid-scale storage with separately scalable energy and power
Flow battery – automotive starting and UPS
x: Lead-acid serves automotive starting and UPS; flow batteries suit grid-scale storage and NMC (not LFP) has a nickel-manganese-cobalt cathode.

s: What is the electrolyte of a lead-acid battery?
x: Lead-acid batteries use lead and PbO2 with sulphuric acid; KOH is the Ni-Cd electrolyte.

s: Which battery, in which a metal hydride replaces cadmium, is used in hybrid vehicles?
x: In NiMH batteries a metal hydride replaces cadmium; they are used in hybrid vehicles.

s: Which electrolyte is used in a nickel-cadmium (Ni-Cd) battery?
x: A Ni-Cd cell has a nickel oxide hydroxide cathode, a cadmium anode and potassium hydroxide (KOH) electrolyte.

s: In a lithium-ion battery, what is graphite generally used as?
x: Graphite is the anode of a lithium-ion battery; lithium, nickel and cobalt are used in the cathode.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding sodium-ion batteries is NOT correct?
o: They can be used for low-cost energy storage.
They avoid cobalt, nickel and copper in the stated chemistry.
They are being considered for low-cost electric vehicles.
Their volumetric energy density is higher than that of LFP batteries.
x: The volumetric energy density of sodium-ion batteries is still below that of LFP batteries. The other statements describe their stated advantages or applications.

s: Sodium-ion batteries are being promoted in the storage debate primarily as which of the following?
o: A system that cannot be used for stationary storage
A technology requiring more lithium than lithium-ion batteries
A replacement for all pumped storage projects
x: Sodium-ion technology is presented as a safer, mineral-light alternative. It is not described as a universal replacement for pumped storage or as dependent on more lithium.

s: Which battery stores liquid electrolytes in tanks, so that energy and power can be scaled separately?
x: Flow (vanadium) batteries keep liquid electrolytes in tanks and are used for grid-scale storage.

s: Which lithium-ion cathode chemistry is noted for being safe and long-lived?
x: LFP is the safe, long-life Li-ion cathode chemistry; NMC uses nickel, manganese and cobalt.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Solid-state batteries use a solid electrolyte; NiMH replaces cadmium with metal hydride, lead-acid uses sulphuric acid and zinc-carbon is not rechargeable.

s: What is a vehicle that combines an engine with a battery-motor system and can be plugged in for charging called?
x: A PHEV is a hybrid that can be charged externally; a plain HEV combines engine and battery-motor but is not plugged in.

s: In which Union Budget was India's battery swapping policy announced?
x: The battery swapping policy was announced in Budget 2022-23; PM E-DRIVE replaced FAME-II in 2024.

s: What is India's goal for EV penetration by 2030?
x: The goal is 30 percent EV penetration by 2030, against about 8.5 percent with over 25 lakh registrations in FY 2025-26.

s: What is the principal energy conversion in a fuel-cell electric vehicle (FCEV)?
o: Hydrogen into electricity on board, with water as the exhaust
Compressed air into electricity, with carbon dioxide as the exhaust
Battery energy into hydrogen, producing water as a by-product
Petrol into electricity through an external generator
x: An FCEV converts hydrogen into electricity on board through a fuel cell, and water is its exhaust product.

s: What is the full form of FCEV, an alternative powertrain vehicle?
x: FCEV is a Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle; BEVs and fuel cell-electric hybrids are also alternative powertrain vehicles.

s: PM E-DRIVE, introduced in 2024, replaced which scheme?
x: PM E-DRIVE replaced FAME-II in 2024.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about vehicle types?
o: A BEV runs on battery only
A PHEV combines an engine with a battery-motor
A plain HEV can be plugged in for charging
An FCEV runs on a hydrogen fuel cell
x: Only the PHEV plugs in; a plain HEV does not.

s: About what share of new vehicle sales in India were electric vehicles in FY 2025-26?
x: India sold over 25 lakh EVs in FY 2025-26, about 8.5% of sales; the goal is 30% by 2030.

s: What share of global lithium processing is concentrated in a few countries?
x: More than 70% of lithium processing (and most cobalt refining) is concentrated in a few countries, a supply-chain risk for battery makers.

s: What is the outlay of the National Critical Mineral Mission, approved in 2025?
x: The Mission's outlay is Rs 16,300 crore; its recycling incentive scheme is Rs 1,500 crore.

s: Where was the lithium resource reported by the Geological Survey of India in February 2023 located?
o: Salal-Haimana in Reasi district, Jammu and Kashmir
x: The GSI reported about 5.9 million tonnes of inferred lithium resources at Salal-Haimana in Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir in 2023. Marlagalla in Mandya, Karnataka, is another Indian lithium occurrence mentioned separately.

s: Rare Earth Corridors were proposed for which group of States?
o: Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
Odisha, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka
Kerala, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra
West Bengal, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
x: The proposed Rare Earth Corridors cover Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

s: KABIL has acquired lithium land in which country?
x: KABIL acquired lithium land in Argentina.

s: Marlagalla, a lithium find in Karnataka, is in which district?
x: Lithium has been found at Marlagalla in Mandya (Karnataka), besides Salal-Haimana in Reasi (J&K).

s: About how much inferred lithium resource did the Geological Survey of India report at Salal-Haimana in Reasi, Jammu and Kashmir?
x: In February 2023 GSI reported about 5.9 million tonnes of inferred lithium at Salal-Haimana, Reasi.

s: Which energy sources and storage mode are combined at the Pinnapuram project?
o: Hydrogen, biomass and battery storage only
x: Greenko’s Pinnapuram project integrates solar and wind generation with pumped storage.

s: The world's first indigenously made high-energy storage device was unveiled in August 2018 at which place in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The device was unveiled at Amaravati on 6 August 2018 (APPSC 2018 key). Pinnapuram in Kurnool hosts Greenko's integrated solar-wind-pumped storage project; Visakhapatnam and Tirupati are not linked to this first.

s: The Pinnapuram integrated solar, wind and pumped storage project is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Pinnapuram (Greenko) is in Kurnool district.

s: How much battery storage does the CEA storage plan for Andhra Pradesh (August 2026) envisage?
x: The plan has 3,931 MW of battery and 7,370 MW of pumped storage for AP.

s: For what was the remaining 10 GWh of ACC battery capacity, put to global bids in July 2026, meant?
x: The remaining 10 GWh was put to global bids for grid-scale storage.

s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a hurdle in implementing the ACC battery programme?
x: Visa delays, local-content rules and missing technology were identified as hurdles. Shortage of pumped-storage reservoirs was not listed as an ACC programme hurdle.

s: Which Ministry runs the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
x: The ACC programme (approved 12 May 2021, 50 GWh, Rs 18,100 crore) is run by the Ministry of Heavy Industries.

s: What capacity and outlay does the PLI scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell batteries have?
x: The ACC-PLI, approved on 12 May 2021, covers 50 GWh with an outlay of ₹18,100 crore.

s:
Consider the following statements about the PLI scheme for ACC batteries:
1. It was approved on 12 May 2021.
2. Ola Electric was allotted 20 GWh.
3. Reliance was allotted 20 GWh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The scheme was approved on 12 May 2021 and Ola Electric got 20 GWh; Reliance got 15 GWh, not 20 GWh.

s: Which of the following gigafactory pairs is correctly matched?
x: Ola Electric's gigafactory is at Krishnagiri (Tamil Nadu); Reliance's is at Jamnagar (Gujarat).

s: Why is energy storage regarded as a major bottleneck in integrating renewable energy into the power system?
o: Renewable energy can never be connected to a grid without coal generation.
Storage helps balance variable renewable generation and supports round-the-clock renewable electricity.
Storage eliminates the need for electricity transmission networks entirely.
Renewable energy is available only during peak electricity demand.
x: Storage addresses the variability of renewable generation and helps provide 24×7 renewable electricity. It does not eliminate the need for grids or imply that renewable energy is never grid-compatible.

s: Under the Energy Storage Obligation, how was the share of energy that DISCOMs must meet through storage to rise?
x: The Energy Storage Obligation provided for a rise from 1 percent in 2023-24 to 4 percent in 2029-30.

s: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026, which emphasises BESS, hybrid renewable energy, smart grids and Time-of-Day tariffs, is meant to replace the National Electricity Policy of which year?
x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 replaces the National Electricity Policy 2005. 2003 is the year of the Electricity Act, not the policy; 2015 is the year of UDAY; 2022 is the year of the Energy Storage Obligation and the Energy Conservation Amendment.

s: Which of the following are policy measures for battery energy storage systems (BESS) in India?
o: Waiver of ISTS charges for co-located storage only
Consumer ownership or leasing of storage only
Recognition of storage as a power-system element only
x: All three are stated measures: ISTS waiver for co-located storage, consumer ownership or leasing, and recognition of ESS as a power-system element.

s: Which place is associated with the world’s largest single-location BESS outside China?
x: Adani Green commissioned the world’s largest single-location BESS outside China at Khavda in Gujarat in May 2026.

s: What is India's energy storage requirement by 2029–30 as estimated by the CEA?
x: CEA estimated a need of 336 GWh by 2029–30, against only about 500 MWh of BESS in September 2025.

s: Which Ministry issued the Energy Storage Obligation of 2022?
x: The ESO was issued by the Ministry of Power in 2022; ACC-PLI is under Heavy Industries and battery rules under MoEFCC.

s: About how much battery energy storage capacity had India installed by September 2025?
x: India had only about 500 MWh of BESS by September 2025, against a CEA need of 336 GWh by 2029-30.

s: Molten-salt storage is associated with concentrated solar power because it does which of the following?
o: Produces hydrogen directly from atmospheric nitrogen
Stores electricity as rotational kinetic energy
Allows generation after sunset by storing thermal energy
Uses underground caverns to store compressed air
x: Molten salt provides thermal storage in concentrated solar power plants, enabling electricity generation after sunset.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pumped storage — energy stored as rotational kinetic energy in a flywheel
Compressed air storage — air compressed into caverns and later expanded through turbines
Flywheel storage — surplus water pumped uphill
Molten salt storage — hydrogen converted into electricity on board
x: Compressed air storage does compress air into caverns and later expand it through turbines. The other pairs are swapped: rotational kinetic energy describes a flywheel, not pumped storage; pumping water uphill is pumped storage, not a flywheel; and converting hydrogen to electricity on board is a fuel-cell vehicle, not molten-salt storage, which stores heat in concentrated solar plants.

s: In which State is Tehri PSP, India's first variable-speed pumped storage project?
x: Tehri PSP (4 x 250 MW) in Uttarakhand is India's first variable-speed pumped storage project.

s: How does Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) work?
o: Compressing air into caverns and expanding it through turbines
Storing energy as rotational kinetic energy
Pumping water uphill for release at peak
x: CAES compresses air into caverns and later expands it through turbines; a flywheel stores rotational kinetic energy.

s: Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, which of the following is prohibited for producers?
o: Disposing of waste batteries in landfills
Using recycled material in new batteries
x: Producers must collect, recycle or refurbish waste batteries and use recycled material; landfill disposal is prohibited.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Battery Pack Aadhaar (BPAN)?
o: It is mandatory for industrial batteries exceeding 2 kWh
It is mandatory for electric vehicle batteries
It is mandatory for portable batteries of every capacity
It does not cover all household electrical appliances
x: BPAN is mandatory only for EV batteries and industrial batteries above 2 kWh, not every portable battery.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022?
o: They replaced the Batteries (Management and Handling) Rules, 2001
They permit incineration of waste batteries
They ban landfill disposal of waste batteries
x: The Rules ban both landfill disposal and incineration of waste batteries, so permitting incineration is wrong.

s: By which year do the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 set a material recovery target of 90%?
x: The Rules target 90% material recovery by 2026-27.

s: Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, who must collect and recycle waste batteries under Extended Producer Responsibility?
x: Under EPR, producers and importers of batteries must collect and recycle waste batteries.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Sodium vapour lamp — white light and excellent colour rendering
Incandescent lamp — most energy lost as sound
CFL — contains mercury and has a shorter life than LED
LED — high mercury content and substantial heat production
x: CFLs are more efficient than incandescent lamps but contain mercury and have a shorter life than LEDs. Incandescent lamps mainly lose energy as heat, while sodium vapour lamps produce yellow light with poor colour rendering.

s: Which one of the following lamps has the highest efficacy, longest life and no mercury?
x: LED lamps have the highest efficacy and longest life among the listed lamps and do not contain mercury.

s: What is the main emitter material of an LED?
x: Gallium arsenide is the main LED emitter; LEDs contain no mercury.

s: Which lamp gives white light, unlike the yellow light of a sodium vapour lamp?
x: Mercury vapour lamps give white light, while sodium vapour lamps give monochromatic yellow light.

s: Which organisation runs the SAKSHAM fuel-conservation campaign?
x: SAKSHAM is run by the Petroleum Conservation Research Association (PCRA), not BEE.

s: Energy efficiency is linked to sustainable development mainly because it does which of the following?
o: increases the energy intensity of the economy
reduces the need for new energy sources
requires replacing all renewable energy with fossil fuels
has no effect on energy demand
x: Using energy efficiently lowers demand, so fewer new energy sources need to be built (APPSC 2025). It lowers energy intensity rather than raising it, does not require fossil fuels, and directly cuts demand.

s: Which of the following is NOT an energy-conservation practice?
o: Using pressure cookers and lids while cooking
x: Incandescent bulbs lose most energy as heat; LEDs, star-rated appliances and switching off idle loads save energy.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about energy conservation observances and awards?
o: National Energy Conservation Day is observed on 14 December
National Energy Conservation Week is 14–20 December
The National Energy Conservation Awards are given by MNRE
The National Energy Conservation Awards were instituted in 1991
x: NECA is given by BEE under the Ministry of Power, not by MNRE.

s: Where is Andhra Pradesh's model Super ECBC building located?
x: The AP model Super ECBC building is located at Sagar Nagar in Visakhapatnam.

s: During National Energy Conservation Week in Andhra Pradesh in 2024, which department collaborated in the awareness activities?
x: The School Education Department collaborated in Andhra Pradesh’s National Energy Conservation Week awareness activities in 2024.

s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh State Energy Conservation Mission (APSECM) constituted?
x: APSECM was constituted in 2012.

s: Which is India's first standalone State Designated Agency of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency?
x: APSECM is India's first standalone State Designated Agency of BEE and enforces the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Where was the first IoT energy pilot of APSECM at an MSME unit undertaken?
x: The IoT energy pilot was first undertaken at an MSME unit in East Godavari and was later extended to all districts with BEE.

s: In which year were the National Energy Conservation Awards instituted?
x: NECA was instituted in 1991 and is given by BEE under the Ministry of Power.

s: Which State/UT stood first in the National Energy Conservation Awards 2025?
x: Chandigarh came first in the National Energy Conservation Awards 2025, given by BEE under the Ministry of Power.

s: How many industries in Andhra Pradesh are covered under the PAT scheme?
x: In AP, 59 industries are under PAT, saving about 1.16 Mtoe; ECBC is applied in 123 ULBs.

s: The inaugural State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index was prepared by which of the following combinations?
o: NITI Aayog with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency
Bureau of Energy Efficiency with the Energy Efficiency Services Limited
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change with NITI Aayog
Bureau of Energy Efficiency with the Alliance for an Energy Efficient Economy
x: The inaugural State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index, introduced in 2018, was prepared by NITI Aayog in association with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State Energy Efficiency Index (SEEI)?
o: It was developed by BEE with the Alliance for an Energy Efficient Economy
It classifies States into only three categories
Front Runner is one of its categories
It forms the basis for the National Energy Conservation Awards
x: SEEI uses four categories: Front Runner, Achiever, Contender and Aspirant.

s: In the inaugural State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index (2018), Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category?
x: Andhra Pradesh was rated a Front Runner, the top category, in the inaugural 2018 index prepared by NITI Aayog with BEE (APPSC 2018). Achiever, Contender and Aspirant are the lower categories.

s: Which organisation prepared the Energy Efficiency Implementation Readiness ranking (November 2016), in which Andhra Pradesh came first?
x: The World Bank (with EESL) prepared it; AP was first (42.01) and Rajasthan second.

s: In SEEI 2024, which State led the 5–15 Mtoe group?
x: AP led the 5–15 Mtoe group; Maharashtra (>15), Assam (1–5) and Tripura (<1) led the others.

s: Under the State Energy Efficiency Index, what score must a 'Front Runner' State exceed?
x: SEEI categories are Front Runner (>60%), Achiever, Contender and Aspirant.

s: In the State Energy Efficiency Index 2024, which State led the group of States with energy demand above 15 Mtoe?
x: In SEEI 2024 (BEE with AEEE), Maharashtra led the >15 Mtoe group, AP the 5–15 group, Assam the 1–5 group and Tripura the <1 group.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Energy Conservation Act, 2001 – Energy audits of designated consumers
Bureau of Energy Efficiency – Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Carbon Credit Trading Scheme – Original Energy Conservation Act, 2001
x: The 2001 Act provides for energy audits of designated consumers (and penalties); BEE is under the Ministry of Power, ECO Niwas covers residential buildings and the CCTS basis came with the 2022 amendment.

s: When did the Bureau of Energy Efficiency become operational?
x: BEE became operational on 1 March 2002.

s: Under the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022, designated consumers must use a minimum share of which energy?
x: The 2022 amendment requires designated consumers to use a minimum share of non-fossil energy.

s: When did the Rajya Sabha pass the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022, completing its passage?
x: The Lok Sabha passed the Bill in August 2022 and the Rajya Sabha in December 2022, completing its passage.

s: The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022 provides a legal basis for which of the following?
o: A mandatory market for petroleum imports
A separate market for nuclear fuel
x: The 2022 amendment gave legal basis to a carbon market through the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme.

s: Under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, energy-efficiency norms apply to buildings with a connected load above what limit?
x: Norms apply to buildings with connected load over 100 kW or contract demand over 120 kVA.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022:
1. It extended energy codes to large residential buildings.
2. It allows efficiency norms to be set for vehicles and vessels.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 2022 amendment extended building codes to large residential buildings and enabled efficiency norms for vehicles and vessels.

s: Under which of the following does the Bureau of Energy Efficiency, a statutory body created by the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, function?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
x: BEE functions under the Ministry of Power; the JV of power PSUs that distributes LEDs is EESL.

s: The Standards and Labelling programme for energy-consuming equipment in India is administered by which organisation under which Ministry?
o: National Productivity Council under the Ministry of Heavy Industries
Energy Efficiency Services Limited under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power
Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: The Standards and Labelling programme is administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power.

s: Which organisation implements both UJALA and the Street Lighting National Programme?
x: Both programmes are implemented by Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL), a joint venture of public-sector undertakings under the Ministry of Power.

s: About what share of its oil does India import?
x: India imports about 80% of its oil, so cheap demand reduction through efficiency improves energy security.
