s: The National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency is one of how many missions under NAPCC (2008)?
x: NMEEE is one of the eight missions of the National Action Plan on Climate Change (2008).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about fuel-efficiency and conservation initiatives?
o: SAKSHAM is a fuel-conservation drive of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency
The first CAFE norms were notified in 2017
CAFE norms set average fuel-efficiency targets for M1 cars
The Bureau of Energy Efficiency enforces the CAFE norms
x: SAKSHAM is conducted by the Petroleum Conservation Research Association (PCRA), not BEE.

s: Under which Section of the Energy Conservation Act is India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, notified in 2023, provided for?
x: Section 14AA provides for the CCTS, India's first mandatory compliance carbon market.

s: Under the star-labelling changes effective from 1 January 2026, when may manufacturers be penalised?
o: the product receives fewer than three stars irrespective of its actual consumption
actual energy consumption deviates from the declared label rating
a product is sold without an international energy certificate
the product is manufactured outside a designated consumer sector
x: Manufacturers may be penalised if the actual energy consumption of a product deviates from the consumption declared through its label.

s: Under BEE's Standards and Labelling programme, about how much energy does each additional star save?
x: The one-to-five-star programme (over 40 equipment types) saves about 10–15 per cent energy per additional star.

s: Which of the following is under the voluntary star-labelling list?
x: Industrial motors, computers and microwave ovens are voluntary; ceiling fans, refrigerators and tubular fluorescent lamps are mandatory.

s: In which year was BEE's Standards and Labelling programme launched?
x: The S&L programme was launched in 2006 and rates over 40 equipment on a 1–5 star scale.

s: ECO Niwas Samhita, introduced in 2018, is an energy code for which of the following?
x: ECO Niwas Samhita (2018) covers residential buildings; ECBC (2007) covers new commercial buildings.

s:
Consider the following statements about building codes:
1. ECBC (2007) covers new commercial buildings.
2. ECO Niwas Samhita covers commercial buildings.
3. ECSBC (2024) adds sustainability to the code.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: ECBC covers commercial buildings and ECSBC adds sustainability; ECO Niwas Samhita is for residential buildings.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: ECO Niwas Samhita – New commercial buildings
x: ECBC applies to new commercial buildings; ECO Niwas Samhita applies to residential buildings, and ECSBC adds sustainability to the framework.

s: Which organisation runs the National Efficient Cooking Programme, which distributes induction stoves?
x: EESL, a joint venture of Ministry of Power PSUs, runs the National Efficient Cooking Programme along with UJALA and SLNP.

s: In which year were UJALA and the Street Lighting National Programme both launched?
x: Both UJALA and the Street Lighting National Programme were launched in January 2015.

s: The Street Lighting National Programme primarily replaced older street lighting based on which technology with LEDs?
x: Under the Street Lighting National Programme, older sodium vapour street lights were replaced by LED lights.

s: Under UJALA, approximately how many LED bulbs have been distributed?
x: UJALA distributed about 36.86 crore LED bulbs, along with 72.18 lakh LED tube lights and 23.59 lakh energy-efficient fans. 9.5 crore is the number of PMUY LPG connections.

s: ADEETIE, launched in July 2025 with an outlay of ₹1,000 crore, promotes energy efficiency in which sector?
x: ADEETIE focuses on energy efficiency among MSMEs through audits and financial support.

s: How many clusters and sectors does ADEETIE, the MSME energy-efficiency scheme, cover?
x: ADEETIE covers 60 clusters in 14 sectors; 478 units in 8 sectors is PAT Cycle I.

s: What is the full form of UJALA?
o: Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All
Ujjwal Jyoti for All Lighting Access
Universal Jyoti through Affordable LED Appliances
Unnat Jeevan by Affordable Lighting for All
x: UJALA stands for Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All, launched by EESL in January 2015.

s: What interest subvention does the ADEETIE scheme give to micro and small enterprises for energy-efficiency loans?
x: ADEETIE (July 2025, ₹1,000 crore) gives 5% interest subvention to micro and small units and 3% to medium units.

s: Which body is the regulator of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme?
x: CERC is the regulator, while BEE is the administrator of the scheme.

s: What is the Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme?
o: A market mechanism setting energy-reduction targets for designated consumers
A labelling programme for household appliances
A loan scheme for solarising farm pumps
A scheme for distributing LED bulbs to households
x: PAT is a market mechanism under NMEEE that assigns energy-reduction targets to designated consumers.

s: Where are Energy Saving Certificates (ESCerts) under the PAT scheme traded?
x: Over-achievers earn ESCerts and under-achievers buy them on power exchanges, including the Indian Energy Exchange.

s: After the expansion of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), PAT is proposed to retain which four residual sectors?
o: Chlor-alkali, cement, railways and domestic buildings
Iron and steel, petrochemicals, refineries and pulp and paper
Thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings
x: The proposed four residual PAT sectors are thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings.

s: Which certificates are issued under PAT and CCTS, respectively?
x: PAT is associated with energy-intensity certificates (ESCerts), while CCTS issues emission-intensity certificates called CCCs.

s: By how much does India aim to cut the emission intensity of its GDP by 2030 over 2005 levels, a target the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme supports?
x: The stated goal is a 45% cut in GDP emission intensity by 2030 relative to the 2005 level.

s: What does the compliance mechanism of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme cover?
o: 9 heavy industries with GHG intensity targets for 208 units
4 sectors: thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings
x: CCTS covers 9 heavy industries, with GHG emission-intensity targets for 208 units. 478 units in 8 sectors was PAT Cycle I; the four sectors are those PAT will retain; 60 clusters in 14 sectors is ADEETIE.

s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the original PAT sectors?
x: The original PAT sectors included thermal power, chlor-alkali and textiles. Railways was added later and is part of the proposed residual-sector arrangement.

s: From which date does the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, which recognised India's CCTS, apply?
x: The UK CBAM applies from 1 January 2027; in September 2026 the UK recognised India's CCTS as a qualifying carbon price.

s: How many units and sectors did PAT Cycle I (2012-15) cover?
x: PAT-I covered 478 units in 8 sectors; 208 units/9 industries is CCTS and 60 clusters/14 sectors is ADEETIE.

s: Up to how much free electricity can households receive under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana?
x: The scheme provides for free power of up to 300 units per month, with beneficiary households becoming prosumers.

s: Under PM Surya Ghar, what share of the cost for the first 2 kW does Central Financial Assistance cover?
x: CFA covers 60% of the cost for 2 kW and 40% for additional capacity up to 3 kW.

s: What is the household target of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana by March 2027?
x: The scheme targets rooftop solar installations in 1 crore households by FY 2026-27, that is, March 2027.

s: What is the outlay of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana?
x: PM Surya Ghar has an outlay of ₹75,021 crore.

s: Which scheme provides for one Model Solar Village in every district and is called the world's largest domestic rooftop solar scheme?
o: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
x: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (February 2024) has one Model Solar Village per district and is the world's largest domestic rooftop solar scheme.

s: How much rooftop solar capacity is PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana expected to add?
x: PM Surya Ghar aims at about 30 GW of rooftop solar in 1 crore households.

s: What is the aim of UDAY, introduced in November 2015?
o: Financial turnaround of state electricity distribution companies
x: UDAY (Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana) was introduced by the Ministry of Power in November 2015 for the financial turnaround of state discoms.

s: To what level did UDAY aim to reduce AT&C losses by 2018-19?
x: UDAY targeted AT&C losses of 15% and a zero ACS-ARR gap by 2018-19.

s: What are the national targets of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS)?
o: AT&C losses of 12–15% and an ACS-ARR gap of zero
AT&C losses of zero and an ACS-ARR gap of 12–15%
AT&C losses of 30% and an ACS-ARR gap of 15%
Only reduction of transmission losses, without an ACS-ARR target
x: RDSS aims at pan-India AT&C losses of 12–15% and an ACS-ARR gap of zero.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UDAY?
o: States took over 75% of DISCOM debt outstanding as on 30 September 2015
The arrangement covered only half of total outstanding DISCOM debt
50% of the debt was taken over in 2015-16
25% of the debt was taken over in 2016-17
x: The arrangement covered 97% of total outstanding DISCOM debt.

s: What is the outlay of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS)?
x: RDSS has an outlay of ₹3,03,758 crore; ₹75,021 crore is PM Surya Ghar.

s: Under UDAY, States took over what share of discom debt?
x: States took over 75% of discom debt: 50% in 2015-16 and 25% in 2016-17.

s: The States that joined UDAY together accounted for about what share of total DISCOM debt?
x: The States participating in UDAY covered about 97% of total DISCOM debt.

s: Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (Saubhagya) was launched in which year, and for what purpose?
x: Saubhagya was launched in 2017 for universal household electrification. Urban distribution strengthening is IPDS (2014), DISCOM turnaround is UDAY (2015) and farm-pump solarisation is PM-KUSUM (2019).

s: What does the Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS), launched in December 2014, mainly aim to strengthen?
o: Rural agricultural feeder separation and village electrification
Urban sub-transmission and distribution, metering and IT enablement
x: IPDS strengthens urban sub-transmission and distribution, metering and IT enablement.

s: Which of the following scheme–ministry pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (2016) – Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (2024) – MNRE
x: PM-KUSUM was launched by MNRE, not the Ministry of Power (which runs UDAY).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Grameen Vitrak Yojana was launched in 2009
The Grameen Vitrak Yojana raised the rural share of LPG distributors from 18% to 60%
Surya Nutan is an indoor solar stove launched in 2022
Surya Nutan was developed by EESL
x: Surya Nutan was developed by IOCL, not EESL.

s: IPDS subsumed which earlier programme?
x: The Integrated Power Development Scheme subsumed the Restructured Accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programme (R-APDRP).

s: In which year was the Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) launched?
x: DDUGJY was launched in December 2014 by the Ministry of Power for rural distribution and feeder separation.

s: As per the latest figure, how many willing households were electrified under Saubhagya?
x: Saubhagya electrified 2.86 crore willing households; 2.82 crore was an older figure (March 2021).

s: Which village in Manipur was identified as the last village to be electrified?
x: Leisang in Manipur was identified as the last village to be electrified.

s: Separation of agricultural and non-agricultural feeders is a feature of which scheme?
x: DDUGJY separates agricultural and non-agricultural feeders and strengthens rural networks; IPDS is urban.

s: Which earlier rural electrification scheme was subsumed in DDUGJY?
x: DDUGJY (December 2014) subsumed the Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana (RGGVY); IPDS subsumed R-APDRP.

s: What does Component C of PM-KUSUM relate to?
o: Decentralised grid-connected solar plants on barren land
Solarisation of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps
x: Component C solarises grid-connected agricultural pumps. Component A covers decentralised grid-connected solar/RE plants on farm or barren land, and Component B covers standalone solar pumps. Urban household rooftop solar comes under PM Surya Ghar, not PM-KUSUM.

s: What is the subsidy-sharing pattern for Components B and C of PM-KUSUM?
x: For Components B and C, the Centre contributes 30%, the State 30% and the farmer 40%; a bank loan may also be used by the farmer.

s: What does Component B of PM-KUSUM cover?
o: Grid-connected solar plants on farm land
x: Component B is standalone solar pumps; A is grid-connected plants and C is solarisation of grid-connected pumps.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM-KUSUM?
o: It was launched in 2019 under MNRE
